clusters.pattern: Broadcast wire `message` lost/XX-clobbered/case-flipped, or `service` arg clobbered so the broadcast call dies and the except-handler re-broadcasts with a substituted 'Health check error:/Restart error:' message instead of the documented string
clusters.note: test_broadcast_event_format (backend/tests/unit/core/test_health_monitor.py:657) checks payload keys only, never data['message'] content. Kills cluster via exact-message assertions (drafted T5).

clusters.pattern: event_type_map key or value clobbered (XX…XX, CASE) in _broadcast_status — status->event-type mapping breaks or mislabels recorded events; membership-filtered event tests still pass on other statuses' events
clusters.note: Event tests (:1245-1337) assert any event with expected event_type exists; never that THIS status recorded exactly the right event. Drafted T4 parametrizes all 6 status->event-type pairs.

clusters.pattern: HealthEvent fields clobbered at construction/call site: service=None, message=None/dropped, timestamp=None or now(None) — /api/system/health recent_events (backend/api/routes/system.py:1358) loses service/message/naive timestamp
clusters.note: Event tests filter by e.event_type only; e.service/e.message/e.timestamp never asserted. Killed by drafted T4.

clusters.pattern: WebSocket envelope schema mutations: data.message key renamed (XXmessageXX/MESSAGE) or top-level timestamp made naive via datetime.now(None)
clusters.note: test_broadcast_event_format never touches data['message'] or timestamp tz-awareness. Killed by drafted T4.

clusters.pattern: Exponential backoff formula broken: base/2^(n-1), base*(2*(n-1)), 3^(n-1) base, 2^(n-2) exponent shift — sleep schedule no longer base*2^(n-1)
clusters.note: Existing backoff test (:208) only checks delays are increasing with len>=2. Killed by drafted T1 exact-schedule assertion.

clusters.pattern: Max-retries boundary comparison flipped > to >= — gives up one restart attempt early
clusters.note: Existing test (:264) asserts restart_count <= 2 (upper bound only). Killed by drafted T2 exact-count assertion.

clusters.pattern: Post-restart-success verification/accounting broken (is_healthy=None, count reset =0->=1, sleep(2)->sleep(None), check_health(None)) — masked because the loop's recovery branch later resets counts and broadcasts healthy, so eventual-state assertions pass
clusters.note: Convergence pattern: crash/error paths re-broadcast restart_failed but loop recovers. Killed by drafted T3 direct _handle_failure call with strict assertions.

clusters.pattern: Loop recovery-detection threshold `count > 0` mutated: >=0 spams a recovery broadcast+event on every healthy cycle once the key exists; >1 skips the recovery broadcast for single failures (count stuck at 1)
clusters.note: No test asserts broadcast COUNT or the single-failure recovery broadcast. Needs a cycle-count-timed test (drafted none this wave; kill recipe in dossier notes).

clusters.pattern: _handle_failure(None) arg clobber at both loop call sites — crashes immediately, per-service except re-broadcasts unhealthy and retries with the correct arg; net effect is duplicate unhealthy broadcasts/crash logs, same eventual restart
clusters.note: Convergence pattern. Killable only by 'exactly one unhealthy broadcast per failed cycle' counting assertion (dossier note, no draft this wave).

clusters.pattern: asyncio.create_task name= string clobbered (XXservice-health-monitorXX / SERVICE-HEALTH-MONITOR) — NEM-5057 task name not pinned
clusters.note: Existing task-name test asserts only 'health' in name.lower() and not Task-N. Killed by drafted T6 exact-name assertion.

clusters.pattern: Logger message-text-only mutations (logger.*(None), XX…XX, lower/UPPER case string swaps) across start/stop/loop/handle_failure/broadcast — no control-flow or behavior change
Log-level / exc_info diagnostics tweaks: exc_info=True -> None/False/dropped on exception logs; log_level ternary forced-warning (and False) / forced-info (or True) / flipped (!=)
clusters.note: Affects only log verbosity/tracebacks; no behavior or wire change.

clusters.pattern: break -> return in CancelledError handler — sole difference is skipping the final 'Health check loop stopped' log line

Non-behavioral argument-removal artifacts: logger.warning(msg) -> logger.warning() inside the broadcast-failure except (TypeError raised and swallowed by the outer per-service guard; monitor keeps running) and get_recent_events default limit 50 -> 51 (one extra event max from a 100-deque, no spec depends on exactly 50)
clusters.note: bs#72 is a real crash in the exception handler but fully masked by the loop guard; gre#1 is a default-tweak nobody should assert.
